stem: A depositor invests Rs 4,000 at the end of every 6 months for 2 years. The bank compounds interest at a nominal annual rate of 8% compounded half-yearly. What is the future value of this annuity at the end of 2 years?  [Given: (1.04)^4 = 1.1699]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Simply totalling four half-yearly deposits of Rs 4,000 without compounding gives Rs 16,000, ignoring all interest earned.
Treating the Rs 8,000 annual equivalent as two annual payments at 8% annual and using n = 2 gives FV = 8000 x (1.1664-1)/0.08 = Rs 16,640; this mismatches the actual half-yearly payment frequency.

Using the full nominal annual rate of 8% as the per-period rate and 4 periods gives (1.08)^4 = 1.3605; FV = 4000 x (1.3605-1)/0.08 = Rs 18,025, which over-compounds because the period rate was not halved.

explanation: The decisive move is converting the nominal annual rate to the half-yearly period rate before applying the annuity formula. Period rate i = 8%/2 = 4% = 0.04, n = 4 half-years. FV = A x [(1+i)^n - 1]/i = 4000 x (1.1699 - 1)/0.04 = 4000 x 4.2475 = Rs 16,990.

explanation_sections.punchline: Match the payment frequency to the compounding period - divide the nominal annual rate by 2 to get the per-half-year rate of 4%.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: FV = A x [(1+i)^n - 1]/i. Step 1 (the decisive move): convert rate - i = 8%/2 = 0.04 per half-year, n = 2 years x 2 = 4. Step 2: apply hint (1.04)^4 = 1.1699. Step 3: FV = 4000 x 0.1699/0.04 = 4000 x 4.2475 = Rs 16,990.
explanation_sections.lesson: When payments are more frequent than annual, always convert both the rate and number of periods to match the payment interval before computing FV.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 seconds. One rate conversion then direct formula. Trap: option 4 uses full 8% as the period rate.
